title: Muscles of the sole of the foot: fourth layer (plantar)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Three muscles, from the medial sides of metatarsals 3 to 5.
Medial sides of the bases of the proximal phalanges of toes 3 to 5.
Adduct toes 3 to 5 toward the second toe and flex their metatarsophalangeal joints.

structures.name: Dorsal interossei muscles of the foot
prompts: Dorsal interossei muscles of the foot

rows: Four muscles, each from the facing sides of two neighboring metatarsals.
First: medial side of the proximal phalanx of the second toe. Second to fourth: lateral sides of the proximal phalanges of toes 2 to 4.
Abduct toes 2 to 4 away from the line of the second toe and flex their metatarsophalangeal joints.
hy: DAB and PAD as in the hand, but the axis of the foot is the second toe: Dorsal interossei ABduct, Plantar interossei ADduct.

rows: Head and upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
Base of the first metatarsal and the medial cuneiform. Its tendon passes behind the lateral malleolus and crosses the sole in the groove of the cuboid.
Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes it. Supports the transverse arch of the foot.
Interosseous membrane and the adjoining posterior surfaces of the tibia and fibula.
Tuberosity of the navicular, with slips to the cuneiforms, the cuboid, and the bases of the second to fourth metatarsals.
Plantarflexes and inverts the foot. It is the main muscular support of the medial longitudinal arch.
hy: Behind the medial malleolus, from front to back: Tibialis posterior, flexor Digitorum longus, posterior tibial Artery and Vein, tibial Nerve, flexor Hallucis longus (Tom, Dick And Very Nervous Harry).
